title: DistGNN: Distributed Graph Neural Network Training for Billion-Scale Graphs
problem: Training large-scale Graph Neural Network models on billion-scale graphs requires significant distributed computation while managing communication overhead across multiple nodes. Current approaches struggle with scalability and efficiency when synchronizing gradients across clusters.
motivation: Billion-scale graphs are prevalent in real-world applications, but existing distributed GNN training systems face communication bottlenecks that limit scalability and efficiency, necessitating novel communication-reduction strategies.
method: DistGNN reduces training overhead using hierarchical sampling—processing only the most important neighboring nodes at each layer instead of all neighbors—which cuts computation. It splits the graph across multiple machines (graph partitioning) so most data stays local rather than being repeatedly sent between computers. This combination reduces communication overhead, the expensive step of synchronizing data across the cluster. Critically, the system maintains convergence properties, meaning the model can still reliably reach its best solution despite the distributed setup.
key_novelty: The core contribution is combining hierarchical sampling with graph partitioning to reduce communication between machines during training while preserving convergence—the mathematical guarantee that the distributed model reaches the same solution quality as training on a single machine.
contributions: Hierarchical sampling strategy for efficient distributed GNN training
Graph partitioning approach to localize computation and reduce communication
System design maintaining convergence under distributed training constraints
primary_theme: Communication-efficient distributed GNN training at scale
